q-19160.name: Question 1
q-19160.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the average rate of change, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(3)-f(-2)}{3-(-2)} \\  & =\frac{(p+10)-(2p-1)}{3+2} \\  & =\frac{11-p}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we know that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=3$ on the interval $[-2,3].$ Thus, 

$$
\frac{11-p}{5}=3.
$$

Solving for $p,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{11-p}{5} & =3 \\ 11-p & =15 \\ -p & =15-11 \\ -p & =4 \\ p & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-19160.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the following table of values for f(x). Knowing that the average rate of change of the function f(x) on the interval [−2,3] is 3, find the value of p.

x −5 −2 0 1 3 5 7
f(x) −11 2p−1 −5 4 p+10 7 8
a
p=5
b
p=−3
c
p=3
d
p=−4
e
p=4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the formula for the average rate of change, we get

ΔfΔx=f(b)−f(a)b−a=f(3)−f(−2)3−(−2)=(p+10)−(2p−1)3+2=11−p5.

Now, we know that ΔfΔx=3 on the interval [−2,3]. Thus, 11−p5=3.

Solving for p, we have

11−p5=311−p=15−p=15−11−p=4p=−4.

q-101731.name: Question 2
q-101731.worked_solution:
We have $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ if and only if $Δf=0.$ So

$$
\begin{aligned} & Δf=0 \\  & f(b)-f(a)=0 \\  & f(b)=f(a).\end{aligned}
$$

This means we have to find an interval  $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$

Since $f(8)=f(14)=6,$ we conclude that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ on the interval $[8,14].$

q-101731.html:
Question 2
?

Find an interval where the average rate of change of f(x) equals 0 given the following table of values of f(x):

x 2 4 6 8 10 12 14
f(x) 4 −3 2 6 −4 1 6
a
[6,8]
b
[8,14]
c
[4,12]
d
[2,10]
e
There is no such interval
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We have ΔfΔx=0 if and only if Δf=0. So Δf=0f(b)−f(a)=0f(b)=f(a).

This means we have to find an interval [a,b] such that f(a)=f(b).

Since f(8)=f(14)=6, we conclude that ΔfΔx=0 on the interval [8,14].

q-101733.name: Question 3
q-101733.worked_solution:
We have $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ if and only if $Δf=0.$ So

$$
\begin{aligned} & Δf=0 \\  & f(b)-f(a)=0 \\  & f(b)=f(a).\end{aligned}
$$

This means we have to find an interval  $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$

Since $f(-2)=f(0)=-1,$ we conclude that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ on the interval $[-2,0].$
